component.name: Spade65
component.summary: Configure a non-QMK Noir Spade65 keyboard

description.p: Spade65 is an independent, clean-room configuration tool for the non-QMK Noir Spade65 keyboard. It remaps keys across the normal, Fn1 and Fn2 layers, records macros, sets built-in and per-key lighting, streams real-time and audio-reactive effects, and adjusts debounce.

Every write is checked against the keyboard's own HID report descriptor before it is sent, so an interface that cannot accept a report is never written to. Firmware flashing, bootloader access and arbitrary HID packets are deliberately not implemented.

ul.li: Configuration works over the wired USB connection. Press Fn+Tab on the keyboard to enter wired mode.
The 2.4 GHz receiver and Bluetooth are recognised but read-only: those transports carry no configuration endpoint, so the keyboard can be identified over them but not changed.
A udev rule is required for access to the keyboard without root, and a sandboxed application cannot install one. The rule ships in the project repository and has to be installed on the host once.

description.p: The device list now explains an empty interface list instead of rendering nothing over the 2.4 GHz receiver.
The battery badge reports what it knows and where the reading came from, rather than hiding itself when there is no reading.
Bluetooth is recognised as a read-only transport with battery reporting, and an audio-reactive spectrum bar can reach the top keyboard row.
